service.description: The Entity Extraction API is a named entity extraction & linking API that performs greatly even on short texts, something that many other similar services cannot do. With this API you will be able to automatically tag your texts, extract Wikipedia entities and enrich your data.

optional_parameters.description: The language of the text to be annotated; currently English, French, German, Italian and Portuguese are supported. Leave this parameter out to let the Entity Extraction API automatically detect the language for you. [de | en | fr | it | pt | auto]
optional_parameters.name: lang

optional_parameters.description: Removes from the output entities having a spot shorter than the specified minimum length. [2 .. +inf]
optional_parameters.name: min_length

optional_parameters.default: types, categories, abstract, lod, image, alternate_labels
optional_parameters.description: Returns more information on annotated entities. "types": adds type information from DBpedia. Types are extracted from the DBpedia of the language specified by the lang parameter. Please notice that different DBpedia instances may contain different types for the same resource. "categories": adds category information from DBpedia/Wikipedia. "abstract": adds the text of the Wikipedia abstract. "image": adds a link to an image depicting the tagged entity, as well as a link to the image thumbnail, served by Wikimedia. Please check the licensing terms of each image on Wikimedia before using it in your app. "lod": adds links to equivalent (sameAs) entities in Linked Open Data repositories or other websites. It currently only supports DBpedia and Wikipedia. "alternate_labels": adds some other names used when referring to the entity.
optional_parameters.name: include

optional_parameters.description: Enables special hashtag parsing to correctly analyze tweets and facebook posts.
optional_parameters.name: social.hashtag

optional_parameters.default: The doctor says an apple is better than an orange
optional_parameters.description: The text you want to annotate. One of (text|html|url|html_fragment) is mandatory.
optional_parameters.name: text

optional_parameters.description: The threshold for the confidence value; entities with a confidence value below this threshold will be discarded. Confidence is a numeric estimation of the quality of the annotation, which ranges between 0 and 1. A higher threshold means you will get less but more precise annotations. A lower value means you will get more annotations but also more erroneous ones.
optional_parameters.name: min_confidence

optional_parameters.description: With this parameter you enable special mention parsing to correctly analyze tweets and facebook posts.
optional_parameters.name: social.mention

optional_parameters.description: This parameter specifies the country which we assume VAT and telephone numbers to be coming from. This is important to get correct results, as different countries may adopt different formats. [AD, AE, AM, AO, AQ, AR, AU, BB, BR, BS, BY, CA, CH, CL, CN, CX, DE, FR, GB, HU, IT, JP, KR, MX, NZ, PG, PL, RE, SE, SG, US, YT, ZW]
optional_parameters.name: country

optional_parameters.description: Returns more information on annotated entities: "phone" enables matching of phone numbers; "vat" enables matching of VAT IDs (Italian only). Note that these parameters require the country parameter to be set, and VAT IDs will work only for Italy. [phone, vat]
optional_parameters.name: extra_types

optional_parameters.description: An URL from which the Entity Extraction API will extract the main content to annotate. The Entity Extraction API will fetch the URL for you, and use an AI algorithm to extract the relevant part of the document to work on; in this case, the main content will also be returned by the API to allow you to properly use the annotation offsets. One of (text|html|url|html_fragment) is mandatory.
optional_parameters.name: url

optional_parameters.description: An HTML snippet from which the Entity Extraction API will remove all HTML tags before analyzing it. One of (text|html|url|html_fragment) is mandatory.
optional_parameters.name: html_fragment

optional_parameters.description: An HTML document from which the Entity Extraction API will extract the main content to annotate, as described in the "url" parameter above.  One of (text|html|url|html_fragment) is mandatory.
optional_parameters.name: html

Dandelion API extracts entities (such as persons, places and events), categorizes and classifies documents in user-defined categories, augments the text with tags and links to external knowledge graphs and more. 

Dandelion API easily scales to support billions of queries per day and can be adapted on demand to support custom and user-defined vocabularies. Additional languages are available on demand.

service.description: Searches as `/v1/search` but returns the articles count per hour or day instead of articles' data

optional_parameters.description: The country to which you want to narrow your search. This parameter is [experimental]. We advise you to use it in conjunction with the `lang` parameter. Accepts any [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) codes
optional_parameters.name: country

optional_parameters.description:
The topic to which you want to restrict the articles of your choice. This parameter is [experimental]. Accepted values are `news`, `sport`, `tech`, `world`, `finance`, `politics`, `business`, `economics`, `entertainment`,`beauty`,`travel`,`music`,`food`,`science`
- `news` usually means a general news feed (main headlines of a website).
> Important: this parameter is [experimental]. Not all news articles are assigned with a `topic`, therefore, we cannot guarantee that 100% of topics talking about technology will be assigned a `tech` label.
> One topic at a time, for example, `topic=sport`
optional_parameters.name: topic

optional_parameters.description:
One or more news resources to filter your search. It should be the normal form of the URL, for example, **[nytimes.com](http://nytimes.com/)**, **[theguardian.com](http://theguardian.com/)**
> Comma separated string, for example `sources=nytimes.com,cnn.com,wsj.com`
optional_parameters.name: sources

optional_parameters.description:
- `day` — default option. Aggregate results by day. No more than 100 days 
- `hour` — Aggregate results by hour. No more than 100 hours
optional_parameters.name: agg_by

optional_parameters.description: Upper boundary of the rank of news website to filter by
optional_parameters.name: to_rank

optional_parameters.description:
Adds to the output of the call two more variables: `media` and `media_content`

Media - the main image published with an article 

media_content  - a comma-separated string of all images used in an article
optional_parameters.name: media

optional_parameters.description:
Specifies the language of the search.  Allowed values are:
`af`, `ar`, `bg`, `bn`, `ca`,`cn`, `cs`, `cy`, `da`, `de`, `el`, `en`, `es`, `et`, `fa`, `fi`, `fr`, `gu`, `he`, `hi`, `hr`, `hu`, `id`, `it`, `ja`, `kn`, `ko`, `lt`, `lv`, `mk`, `ml`, `mr`, `ne`, `nl`, `no`, `pa`, `pl`, `pt`, `ro`, `ru`, `sk`, `sl`, `so`, `sq`, `sv`, `sw`, `ta`, `te`, `th`, `tl`, `tr`,`tw`, `uk`, `ur`, `vi`. 
Specifying the language will make your search more relevant
optional_parameters.name: lang

optional_parameters.description:
One or more sources to be excluded from the search. 
> Comma separated string, for example, `not_sources=nytimes.com,cnn.com,wsj.com`
optional_parameters.name: not_sources

optional_parameters.description: Until which point in time to search for. The default timezone is UTC
optional_parameters.name: to

optional_parameters.description: Limit the search only for the sources which are in top 1 million online websites. Defaults to `True` (`False` if you want to turn it off). Unranked sources are assigned a rank that equals to `999999`
optional_parameters.name: ranked_only

optional_parameters.description:
From which point in time to start the search. No specific format is required. E.g. (`2020/05/01`, `2020-05-01` ,`2020-05-01 12:54:14`, `2020-05-01 4:15am`, `yesterday 2:02 am`, `2020/05/01 12:55 EST`) Default timezone is UTC. **
The default is set to one week ago at midnight UTC.**
optional_parameters.name: from

optional_parameters.description: By default, we search what you specified in `q` in both `title` and `summary` of the article. However, you can limit this to either `title` or `summary`
optional_parameters.name: search_in

optional_parameters.description: Lowest boundary of the rank of news website to filter by. **Important**: lower rank means that a source is more popular
optional_parameters.name: from_rank

required_parameters.description: String to search for. Has to be [URL-encoded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percent-encoding).
required_parameters.name: q
